reference.paraphrase: The ordinary muon decay final state has an electron, a muon neutrino and an electron antineutrino. The electron retains the initial muon's electric charge; the neutrinos are neutral. Charge conservation therefore does not require every disappearance or appearance of a charged particle to occur only as an equal-and-opposite charged pair.
reference.use: Concrete counterexample to source152 universal pair-only wording, not an added lesson exercise or numeric dataset.
